title: Formal Safety Kernel
objective: Implement constitutional safety invariants as a dedicated, testable Rust authority boundary.

stories.title: Artifact identity tokens
stories.outcome: Define cross-platform identity preconditions using device/inode on Unix and volume/file identity plus reparse metadata on Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Identity captures enough information to detect target replacement between plan and execute.
Unsupported identity state lowers authority rather than guessing.
verification: TOCTOU fixtures replace file, directory, symlink, junction, and mount/reparse target between phases.

stories.title: Sealed cleanup plan
stories.outcome: Make every mutating plan immutable, identity-bound, capability-bound, and policy-explained.
acceptance_criteria: Plan records provider/root fingerprint, artifact identity, action class, authority, reversibility, and preconditions.
Execution rejects stale plans after relevant state change.

stories.title: Root and boundary capabilities
stories.outcome: Represent approved roots and filesystem boundaries as explicit capabilities rather than raw paths.
acceptance_criteria: No mutation API accepts an unconstrained raw path.
Cross-root and root-self deletion are impossible through typed APIs.
Mount/reparse boundary behavior is explicit per platform.
verification: Compile-time/API tests plus adversarial boundary fixtures.

stories.title: Action authority lattice
stories.outcome: Implement action classes and Effective Authority as a monotonic minimum over all governing constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Raising user authority cannot raise an artifact above its ceiling.
Unknown/active/protected/partial states collapse to non-destructive authority.
Every authority result has a deterministic explanation trace.

stories.title: Mutation executor isolation
stories.outcome: Make the safety executor the sole code path for filesystem mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Executor revalidates all plan preconditions immediately before mutation.
Partial failures produce explicit per-action results and never hide skipped work.
verification: Static dependency checks and fault-injection tests.
